# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, but I cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. Furthermore, Deaf has not yet seen or described the bomb to us, and arbitrary gestures without established meaning could be misinterpreted ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). 

The manual instructs that the key bearing symbol ᖉ must be pressed first before any other touch on the bomb, followed by cutting a wire according to the light color. Once Deaf inspects the bomb and speaks to describe what markings and keys are present, I can accurately indicate which key matches ᖉ.

Therefore, I will wait for Deaf to observe and describe the bomb.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. Bomb layout: 3 wires (positions 1-3), keypad with 4 slots (1-4, expecting 1 digit), display, and light. Available actions: act(op='cut', position=1..3) or act(op='press', slot=1..4). Since you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, gesture to Deaf what I should do, and Deaf can speak the command aloud for me to execute.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Indicator light is green. Wires are 1: red, 2: yellow, 3: blue. Keypad needs 1 digit. Button 1: backwards capital letter D with flat side on the right. Button 2: vertical hourglass or butterfly shape with rounded loops. Button 3: five squares arranged in an X or plus like a five on a die. Button 4: trident shape or vertical bar with three upward prongs.

I need to instruct Blind, via Deaf, to press Button 1 on the keypad (the button wearing ᖉ, which Deaf identified as Button 1: backwards capital D).

Blind stated the available actions:
`act(op='cut', position=1..3)`
`act(op='press', slot=1..4)`

To convey `press 1` unambiguously to Deaf using the available gesture alphabet:
- 👇 signifies pressing down / press.
- ☝ signifies the number 1 / slot 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: do not touch the bomb yet, wait for my confirmation. Mute: I saw your gesture. To avoid detonating the bomb, please confirm your instruction using two gestures: First gesture is the module: use 👌 for Keypad, or 👊 for Wire. Second gesture is the number: use ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, 🖐 for 4. If multiple actions are needed, send them in sequence.

I will signal Deaf using the requested protocol: `👌` for Keypad and `☝` for Slot 1. 

We only send the keypad press for now because the manual specifies that after the key is pressed first, the light names the cut. Doing this one step at a time allows Deaf to check whether the indicator light changes after Button 1 is pressed before any wire is cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: Blind is pressing Keypad button 1. If any wire needs to be cut, gesture 👊 followed by the wire number (☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3). If no wires need to be cut, gesture 👍.

According to the defusal manual:
1. The key with symbol ᖉ (Button 1) must be pressed first.
2. Next, the light determines which wire to cut. The indicator light is green, which maps to the red wire.
3. Deaf previously identified Wire 1 as red. Therefore, Wire 1 must be cut.

Deaf requested the instruction using the protocol `👊` for Wire followed by the wire number (`☝` for 1).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: I instructed Blind to cut Wire 1. If cutting Wire 1 disarms the bomb completely, gesture 👍.

I will confirm with 👍 to let Deaf know that cutting Wire 1 completes the defusal sequence according to the manual.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
